summary: Mitsuyo Demoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Kyoto University and held an attested post at the University of Marburg in 2024.

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Munich under Helmut Hoffmann and held professorships at Kokugakuin, Tsukuba, and Nihon Universities before directing the Eastern Institute.

Mitsuyuki Ishida studied at Ryukoku University (~1931–1936) and specialized in Buddhist studies. He taught at Ryukoku University from at least 1956, serving as professor from ~1960 to 1976, and was a professor at Shitennoji University in 1976.

Mittal Trivedi is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed an Acharya degree at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (2017–2019). From 2020 to 2024, Trivedi was a doctoral student at the University of Cagliari.
Miyako Notake is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She held part-time lecturer positions at Waseda University, attested in 2015 and 2026.
Miyoko Nakano is a Sinologist who studied at Hokkaido University from ~1952 to 1956. She subsequently held an academic post at Hokkaido University from ~1973 to 1996.

Mizuho Okita specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Tokai University under Katsuhiko Kamimura, completed doctoral work at Gakushuin University under Atsuhiko Yoshida (~2004–2010), and served as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University in 2008.
Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.
Mohammad Ashraf Dar works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a Master of Philosophy from Vikram University, where he also held a post as a research scholar attested in 2014.

Mohammad Habib was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Aligarh Muslim University (~1912–1916), and New College (~1916–1919), and later taught Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi.

Mohan G. Dhadphale specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and editor of Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

Mokurai Shimaji was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū. He served as Geschäftsführer at Nishi Hongan-ji (1870) and 25th head priest at Gankyo-ji (1892–1905), and founded Chiyoda Jogakuen in 1888.

Mona Schrempf specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her doctorate in anthropology at the Free University of Berlin in 2001 and held posts at Heidelberg University and Humboldt University of Berlin in 2006.

Monia Chies is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She completed a master's degree at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 2011 and was a PhD candidate at Humboldt University of Berlin in 2013.

Monica Esposito was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Paris. She held postdoctoral positions at Ca' Foscari, the Sorbonne, and Kansai University, and became an associate professor at Kyoto University in 2003.

Monica L. Smith works in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Michigan (~1990–1997), she taught at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) and became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2002.

Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College (1844–1858) and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1860 to 1887.

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach is an Indologist and linguist who completed her doctorate under Heinz-Jürgen Pinnow at Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at the Universities of Bonn, Bamberg, Cologne, and Heidelberg (1990–2006).
Monika Nowakowska is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She has held academic posts in South Asian studies at the University of Warsaw, attested in 2010 and 2026.

Monika Zin specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Munich, later serving as professor there and at the Free University of Berlin before directing research projects at Leipzig and the Saxon Academy.
